legend: In the Warring States period of ancient China, espionage was the key to survival. An agent named Lian has received a critical mission: to deliver a message from his base in Shanghai (represented on the map by vertex S$$$S$$$) to an allied general in the walled city of Tianjin (vertex T$$$T$$$).

Lian's spymaster warned him: "Our enemies are cunning. They know all the roads and expect an urgent messenger to use the fastest possible path. If you arrive from Shanghai to Tianjin in record time, your identity will be revealed."

The order was clear: calculate the shortest path length, D$$$D$$$, but do not use it. Instead, to pass as a common merchant who might have taken a detour, you must follow a path of length exactly D+1$$$D+1$$$.

To have flexibility and escape routes, Lian needs to know how many travel options meet this condition. Your task is to help him count the number of distinct paths from Shanghai to Tianjin with a length of precisely one more than the minimum.
input: The first line contains four integers N,M,S,$$$N, M, S,$$$ and T$$$T$$$ (1≤N,M≤106,1≤S≠T≤N$$$1 \leq N, M \leq 10^6, 1 \leq S \neq T \leq N$$$), representing the number of cities and roads in China, the starting vertex (S$$$S$$$, Shanghai), and the destination vertex (T$$$T$$$, Tianjin). The next M$$$M$$$ lines each contain two integers ui$$$u_i$$$ and vi$$$v_i$$$ (1≤ui≠vi≤N$$$1 \leq u_i \neq v_i \leq N$$$), indicating that there is a bidirectional road between cities ui$$$u_i$$$ and vi$$$v_i$$$.
output: Print a single integer: the number of distinct paths from Shanghai to Tianjin with a length of one more than the minimum. As this number can be very large, print the result modulo 109+7$$$10^9+7$$$.
note: A path from Shanghai to Tianjin is guaranteed to exist. Multiple roads may exist between the same pair of cities.

Lian 的情报主管警告他：“我们的敌人很狡猾。他们知道所有道路，并预计紧急信使会选择可能的最快路径。如果你以创纪录的时间从上海抵达天津，你的身份就会暴露。”

为了拥有更多的灵活性和逃生路线，Lian 需要知道有多少种出行方案满足这一条件。你的任务是帮助他统计从上海到天津、长度恰好比最短长度多 1 的不同路径数量。
